claim: Under each of ten injected faults (sensor dropout, stale telemetry, corrupted observations, duplicate proposals, clock skew, a frozen agent, judge timeout, network loss, and human-state loss), every authority invariant held in every run: no unsafe commit, no commit without validation, no judgment after a failed validation, an intact event chain, and zero network calls.

evidence.description: invariant no_unsafe_commits holds in every run
invariant no_commit_without_validation_pass holds in every run
invariant every_commit_has_provenance holds in every run
invariant event_chain_intact holds in every run
invariant zero_network_calls holds in every run

limitations: Faults are injected by the simulator; real failures have other signatures and timing.

claim: Routing judgment by agent instability keeps judgment's effect on commits made from degraded evidence.

evidence.detail: mean paired difference 2.55 over 100 pairs, 95% CI [2.34, 2.76]

limitations: Observed mechanism: stale evidence came from a historically stable agent whose sensor dropped out, so the instability signal did not route it to judgment. A routing signal that includes evidence age is the obvious next condition.

claim: Consulting judgment only for agents whose recent proposals were often not committed reduces judgment calls on the Perturbed Mesh.

evidence.detail: supported: mean paired difference -182.2 (100 pairs); 95% CI of the paired difference [-184.3, -180.1] lies below 0

limitations: See instability-routing-preserves-protection: the reduction comes with a loss of protection.
message: evidence is consistent; the status stays as declared until a person changes it

claim: Bounded judgment improves task success on the Perturbed Mesh.

evidence.detail: mean paired difference 0 over 100 pairs, 95% CI [0, 0]

limitations: Recorded as an open hypothesis so the registry shows evidence that does not support it; task success did not change in any paired repetition.
message: evidence is inconsistent with the claim

claim: Across every judge tested (deterministic-only, evidence-heuristic, contrarian, recorded) and every injected fault, judgment was never consulted for a proposal that failed deterministic validation, and no proposal was committed without a passing validation of the same proposal.

evidence.description: invariant no_judgment_after_failed_validation holds in every run
invariant no_commit_without_validation_pass holds in every run
invariant no_judgment_after_failed_validation holds in every run
invariant no_commit_without_validation_pass holds in every run

limitations: This is also enforced by construction (a commit authorization requires a ValidatedProposal) and by property tests; the experiments confirm it on recorded runs, they do not prove it.
The remote Jev condition did not run without credentials and network permission.

claim: On the Perturbed Mesh, adding the evidence-heuristic judgment stage after deterministic validation removed commits made on degraded evidence (observations older than half the staleness limit), at the cost of fewer commits overall, without any unsafe commit; replaying the recorded judgments reproduced the judged condition exactly.

evidence.detail: mean paired difference -2.79 over 100 pairs, 95% CI [-2.94, -2.64]

evidence.description: replayed_judgment reproduces its recorded source exactly
evidence.detail: no replay-fidelity difference recorded for replayed_judgment

limitations: The evidence-heuristic judge is a deterministic rule written to respond to evidence staleness. The result shows what a judgment stage does to the pipeline; it says nothing about how a language model would judge.
One scenario with 100 seeds; seeds vary sensor noise, not the scenario design.
Not yet tested against TypeSafe Jev.

claim: With adaptive gating enabled, background proposals are deferred while the simulated operator-load level is HIGH or CRITICAL, which reduces the number of commits during load perturbations without any unsafe commit.

evidence.detail: supported: mean paired difference -31.92 (50 pairs); 95% CI of the paired difference [-32.49, -31.35] lies below 0

limitations: The operator-load index is simulated (operator_load_v1) and is not a measurement of any person.
Fewer commits is not the same as better outcomes; task progress of background work drops by design.

claim: When the human-state signal is lost just before a load spike, the default signal-loss policy (assume HIGH) keeps background work deferred, whereas holding the last level silently disables gating and increases commits.

evidence.detail: mean paired difference -3.9 over 40 pairs, 95% CI [-4, -3.8]
mean paired difference 12.1 over 40 pairs, 95% CI [12, 12.2]

limitations: This finding motivated changing the default from hold_last to assume_high; it is evidence for that design choice in this simulator only.

claim: In the simulated scenarios tested, deterministic validation with every check enabled prevented every proposal that the independent geometric oracle classified as unsafe from reaching authoritative state, and removing the hazard-clearance check alone was enough to let unsafe proposals through.

evidence.detail: supported: mean paired difference 9.12 (50 pairs); 95% CI of the paired difference [8.9, 9.34] lies above 0

evidence.description: invariant no_unsafe_commits holds in every run

limitations: Simulation only; "unsafe" means a path through a declared circular hazard, a non-finite target, or an out-of-bounds target.
The oracle samples 65 points per path; it is independent of the validator's closed-form geometry but not of the scenario's hazard definitions.
